The psalmist identifies his comfort as God's promise having given him life, not simply the promise itself.
The explanation equates God's judgments of old with what God has done. The verse does not explain them that way.
It asserts how the psalmist would react to people studying God's law, although the text does not say.
Even marked as a guess, the imagined action of the psalmist humming on the road adds a detail the text does not give.
The explanation repeats the answer and fills out the rest with a generic comment about plain words. It lacks Papa Dorin's personality.

The bakery comparison has no clear connection to the psalmist's portion or promise, so the image does not pass the joke logic test.
A half-batch of a heart in an oven mixes images without a clear connection to seeking God with all one's heart.
